# `get_sequence_setting`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Return the autosave and sequence behaviour settings with remaining size and time estimates.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (full command-socket call; shared diagnostic writes; 64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xc1150 (64-bit build), GetAutosaveSetting, GetEnabledPlan; 32-bit build reaches the same GetEnabledPlan/GetAutosaveSetting/EstimateSeqSizeTime; GetEnabledPlan identical (@0x304400/@0x3044e0 64-bit, @0x263458/@0x263508 32-bit); other differences are camera-info and debug reads only |

No params are read. Despite the getter name this is tier C: on the 64-bit build, when the device is on the plan page in exposure mode 2, the query can select the first stored plan as enabled if none is, and it rebuilds the persistent plan-derived settings. It is therefore not safe to use as an observation-only poll. The grade reflects the whole request/reply path, which reaches the shared diagnostic logger; it does not by itself mean the method changes device settings.

Side effects: Rebuilds cached plan settings (strings, flags, coordinates); may set the first stored plan's enable flag; calls frame-size and time estimators whose deeper effects are unresolved. The 32-bit plan selection matches (READ). Every call also performs shared request/reply diagnostic logging.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_sequence_setting"`. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (get_sequence_setting reply (success)) The request method, echoed. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

No handler-specific error is reachable; a failed frame-size lookup is not reported as an error.

## Example

Request, get - Bare request:

```json
{"id":131,"method":"get_sequence_setting"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_sequence_setting","result":{"delay_first":5,"delay_between_frame":2,"group_by_slot":false,"merid_flip":true,"group_name":"Example group","park_mount":true,"shutdown_pi":false,"close_cooler":true,"left_size_m":1500,"left_time_sec":3600},"code":0,"id":131}
```
